title: The Day Joshua Met a Warrior with a Sword
paragraphs:
The Day Joshua Met a Warrior with a Sword
He Thought the Battle Was About Jericho. Then He Came Face to Face with the One Who Was Really in Command.
Most people never realize the greatest battle of their lives is not the one standing in front of them.
It is the one happening inside them.
The night before Jericho fell, Joshua stood staring at walls that looked impossible. Massive. Intimidating. Ancient. The kind of walls that make human beings question everything God promised.
Maybe you've stood before walls like that.
A broken marriage.
A diagnosis.
A financial crisis.
A secret sin nobody knows about.
A prayer that seems unanswered.
A dream that feels buried beneath years of disappointment.
Joshua knew exactly what that felt like.
Israel had crossed the Jordan River. God's promises were finally within reach. Yet between them and the inheritance stood Jericho—fortified, sealed shut, and seemingly unconquerable.
Then something happened that changed everything.
The Bible records:
"Now when Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with a drawn sword in his hand." (Joshua 5:13)
The Hebrew text says the man stood before him with a חֶרֶב שְׁלוּפָה (cherev shelufah)—a sword already drawn from its sheath.
This was not a peaceful traveler.
This was a warrior prepared for battle.
Joshua immediately approached him.
That alone tells us something about Joshua's character.
He did not run.
He did not hide.
He did not send someone else.
He walked directly toward the unknown.
Then he asked one of the most revealing questions in all Scripture:
"הֲלָנוּ אַתָּה אִם־לְצָרֵינוּ"
"Are you for us, or for our adversaries?" (Joshua 5:13)
In modern language:
"Whose side are you on?"
That question still echoes through every generation.
We ask it during elections.
During wars.
During church disagreements.
During family conflicts.
During personal struggles.
"God, are You on my side?"
But Joshua received an answer he never expected.
"לֹא"
"No." (Joshua 5:14)
Not yes.
Not Israel.
Not Jericho.
Simply:
"No."
Imagine the shock.
The warrior continued:
"כִּי אֲנִי שַׂר־צְבָא־יְהוָה"
"But as Commander of the Army of the LORD I have now come."
The Hebrew title is breathtaking.
Sar-Tzeva-YHWH.
Commander of Yahweh's armies.
The highest military authority in heaven.
Suddenly Joshua realized something every believer must eventually learn:
God does not come to take sides.
God comes to take over.
The question was never whether God was on Joshua's side.
The question was whether Joshua was on God's side.
And that changes everything.
Because many of us spend our lives asking heaven to bless our plans while never surrendering to God's plans.
We ask Him to endorse our ambitions.
Approve our desires.
Validate our opinions.
Strengthen our arguments.
Win our battles.
Meanwhile Jesus is asking a completely different question:
"Will you follow Me?"
Not:
"Will I follow you?"
The moment Joshua understood who stood before him, Scripture says:
"Joshua fell facedown to the ground in reverence." (Joshua 5:14)
The Hebrew picture is powerful.
He collapsed.
The warrior had not come to give Joshua strategy first.
He came to receive Joshua's surrender.
That order matters.
Because victory in God's kingdom always begins with submission.
Before walls fall, pride must fall.
Before strongholds collapse, self-reliance must collapse.
Before breakthroughs happen, surrender happens.
Then the Commander spoke words that should sound familiar:
"Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy." (Joshua 5:15)
This was not the first time those words had been spoken.
Centuries earlier, Moses heard nearly the same command at the burning bush.
Many scholars throughout church history have recognized something extraordinary here.
The text strongly suggests this warrior was not merely an angel.
Angels never receive worship.
Angels consistently redirect worship toward God.
Yet this Commander accepts Joshua's reverence.
He speaks with divine authority.
He declares the ground holy because of His presence.
Many theologians identify this encounter as a pre-incarnate appearance of Christ—what is often called a Christophany.
Before Bethlehem.
Before the manger.
Before the cross.
Before the resurrection.
The eternal Son appears as a warrior.
Not because He loves war.
But because He fights for God's redemptive purposes.
The same Jesus who would one day stretch out His hands on a cross first stood before Joshua holding a sword.
The same Savior who said, "Come to Me," also commands the armies of heaven.
Grace and authority.
Mercy and holiness.
Love and justice.
Perfectly united.
This is why the encounter is so unforgettable.
Joshua expected military intelligence.
Instead he received a revelation of God.
He expected battle plans.
Instead he encountered the King.
He thought Jericho was the story.
Jesus was the story.
And maybe that is what some of us need to hear today.
The wall in front of you is not the main story.
The relationship is not the main story.
The struggle is not the main story.
The fear is not the main story.
The addiction is not the main story.
The betrayal is not the main story.
Christ is the story.
Because the greatest miracle in Joshua 5 is not that walls would eventually fall.
The greatest miracle is that a man encountered the living God and was forever changed.
That truth reaches its fullest expression at the cross.
The Gospel is the ultimate story of scandal transformed into grace.
Humanity rebelled.
Humanity sinned.
Humanity chose darkness.
The evidence against us was overwhelming.
If anyone deserved judgment, it was us.
Yet Jesus stepped into our place.
The One holding the sword chose instead to bear the nails.
The Commander became the sacrifice.
The King wore a crown of thorns.
The innocent carried the guilt of the guilty.
The Greek New Testament declares:
"Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν"
"Christ died for our sins." (1 Corinthians 15:3)
Not because we earned it.
Not because we deserved it.
Because grace rewrites everything.
That is the heartbeat of the Gospel.
That is the heartbeat of Joshua's encounter.
That is the heartbeat of our mission.
Because Jesus rewrites everything.
Maybe you came to this article carrying a wall that feels impossible.
A failure you cannot undo.
A regret you cannot erase.
A shame you cannot silence.
A chapter you wish had never happened.
Listen carefully.
Joshua's story was never ultimately about walls.
It was about worship.
Because when a person truly encounters Christ, the walls eventually become secondary.
The greatest victory is discovering who stands with the drawn sword.
The King is still reigning.
The Commander is still leading.
The Savior is still rescuing.
And grace is still rewriting stories every single day.
If this message strengthened your faith, don't let it stop with you.
What wall are you trusting Jesus to bring down?
Your testimony may become the encouragement someone else desperately needs today.
If you desire to glorify God through advancing Gospel-centered ministry, your support truly makes a difference.
Because one encounter with Jesus can change a life.
One surrendered heart can change a family.
One transformed family can change a generation.
And one act of faithfulness can echo into eternity.
The wall was never the biggest thing standing in front of Joshua. The King standing behind him was.
